title: PAL MCP Server — Provider Abstraction Layer (formerly Zen MCP)
redundancy_comparison: Existing: mcp__codex__codex (GPT-5.4) + mcp__gemini-cli__ask-gemini (Gemini 3.1 Pro). PAL adds: Grok, OpenRouter, Ollama, custom models, unified interface, model aliases, provider fallback chains.
description: Provider Abstraction Layer — a single MCP server that enables Claude Code to call Gemini, OpenAI, Grok, OpenRouter, Ollama, and custom models from within a single conversation. Claude stays in control; PAL is invoked when Claude decides another model's perspective is valuable (e.g., code review, synthesis, domain expertise). Supports model aliases, cross-model conversation threading, and a one-command setup script.
stars: ~10.8k (per scriptbyai.com claude code resource list, March 2026)
author: BeehiveInnovations
rebranding_note: Previously 'Zen MCP Server'. Renamed to PAL (Provider Abstraction Layer) in early 2026. lobehub now shows the PAL name.
token_impact: Neutral to slight increase (adds multi-model call overhead, but avoids duplicate MCP registrations for Codex + Gemini if replacing both)
capability_expansion: Adds Grok, OpenRouter, Ollama, custom model support. Unified interface reduces cognitive overhead vs managing two separate MCP tools.
integration_effort: Medium — replaces existing two MCPs (codex, gemini-cli) with one. Requires migration of all codex-researcher and gemini invocations.
risks: Migration cost: all existing codex-researcher subagent + Gemini invocations would need updating
Dependency on third-party MCP vs official Anthropic Codex MCP integration we built
Provider availability: PAL passes through API keys; same availability as underlying providers
Grok/OpenRouter/Ollama support is additive value but not currently needed
The existing Codex MCP is custom-built (claude-mcp-servers/codex-simple/server.js) with multi-turn session support — PAL may not replicate this

comparison_needed.existing_codex: mcp__codex__codex — custom CLI wrapper, GPT-5.4 default from ~/.codex/config.toml, multi-turn via mcp__codex__codex-reply with conversationId
comparison_needed.existing_gemini: mcp__gemini-cli__ask-gemini — Gemini 3.1 Pro, used for UI/visual analysis
comparison_needed.pal_advantage: Unified interface, Grok+Ollama+OpenRouter support, model aliases, one MCP vs two
comparison_needed.pal_disadvantage: Loses multi-turn session tracking of codex-reply; migration cost; community MCP vs custom-built

evaluation.reasoning: High community validation (10.8k stars) and genuine capability expansion (Grok, OpenRouter, Ollama). However, the decisive blocker is whether PAL supports multi-turn conversation threading equivalent to codex-reply with conversationId — the existing Codex MCP's core differentiator for research sessions. If PAL cannot replicate this, migration cost outweighs unified-interface benefit. Integration complexity scored 45 due to mandatory migration of all codex-researcher subagent and Gemini invocations. Current trajectory: if multi-turn is supported, score rises to ~73 (APPROVE); if not, score drops to ~55 (REJECT).

research_questions: Does PAL support multi-turn conversation threading comparable to codex-reply with conversationId?
What is the exact model coverage? Does it support gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4-nano?
Can PAL preserve the custom ~/.codex/config.toml defaults for model selection?
Is there a way to use PAL alongside existing Codex/Gemini MCPs rather than replacing them?
promote_to_approved_if: PAL supports multi-turn conversation threading with session IDs AND supports gpt-5.4/mini/nano model IDs
reject_if: No multi-turn threading support OR migration breaks existing codex-researcher subagent workflow
